slot.brief: Give a straightforward octahedral complex formula and ask for its correct IUPAC name, with ligand-alphabetical-order distractors.

stem: What is the correct IUPAC name of the octahedral complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$?

verdicts.working: The complex ion has charge +1 because of the outer Cl⁻. With neutral NH₃ and two Cl⁻ ligands, cobalt is +3. Ligands are named alphabetically: ammine before chlorido.

working:
Complex charge $=+1$; hence $x-2=+1$, so Co is in oxidation state $+3$.\nLigands are named alphabetically: ammine before chlorido.\nName: tetraamminedichloridocobalt(III) chloride.

Independent check: The complex ion has charge +1 because of the outer Cl⁻. With neutral NH₃ and two Cl⁻ ligands, cobalt is +3. Ligands are named alphabetically: ammine before chlorido.
solution:
The complex ion has charge $+1$; with neutral $\text{NH}_3$ and two $\text{Cl}^-$ ligands, $x-2=+1$, so cobalt is in the $+3$ oxidation state.
Ligands are named alphabetically: ammine before chlorido. Hence the name is tetraamminedichloridocobalt(III) chloride.
